memory_lessons.applicability: For the paired-tile mapping, use the active partial count when assigning an odd final element to its grid-stride CTA.
memory_lessons.claim: The fixed-1024 mapping measured 0.288230 ms; the prior hybrid using ceil(n/4096) capped at 4096 measured 0.304724 ms. The latter was correct but slower, so changing the partial count alone does not imply a speedup.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 1024-capped dynamic count with all required sizes and an odd size exceeding one tile.

proposal.hypothesis: Using ceil(n/4096) partials capped at 1024 preserves the measured 1024-CTA mapping at the largest size while reducing CTA count for smaller inputs. This may lower overhead there, but could also reduce useful parallelism; the full-call effect requires measurement.

retained: Retain the fused absolute-sum, 128-thread paired-tile mapping, aligned float2 path with scalar fallback, CUB CTA reduction, and one-CTA finalizer.
Set partial_count to ceil(n/4096), capped at 1024, and use that active count for both the pair grid stride and finalizer fan-in.
Assign an odd final element using its tile index modulo the active partial count, with an explicit zero-output path for n<=0.
